ICP → 11.4 mg
For sample preparation, an accurately weighed amount of compound, 11.4 mg, was transferred into microwave digestion vials. A minimal volume of concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃) was added, followed by hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) to a total digestion volume of approximately 5 mL. The resulting mixtures were subjected to microwave-assisted digestion at 200 °C for 2 hours to ensure complete decomposition of the organic matrix.
After cooling to room temperature, the digestion mixture was transferred to a 10-mL volumetric flask and diluted to the mark with deionized water. The solution was kept overnight. The solution was transferred into the test tubes.
Initial ICP-OES measurements resulted in signals exceeding the calibration range for cobalt, indicating that the analyte concentration was too high. Therefore, an additional dilution step was performed by transferring 2 mL of the solution into a new test tube and diluting to a final volume of 10 mL with deionized water (dilution factor = 5). These diluted samples were subsequently remeasured.
